questions.stem: One who can speak two languages fluently.
questions.explanation: B is correct. BILINGUAL = fluent in two languages (bi=two + lingual=of language). Compare: monolingual (one), bilingual (two), trilingual (three), multilingual/polyglot (many). A polyglot typically speaks more than two.

questions.stem: A place where books are kept for reading or borrowing but not for sale.
questions.explanation: B is correct. LIBRARY = a place where books and other materials are kept for people to read or borrow, free or at low cost, not for sale. Bookstore/bookshop = books for sale. Archive = historical documents. This is one of the most basic one-word substitution questions.

questions.stem: A doctor who specialises in the care of children.
questions.explanation: C is correct. PAEDIATRICIAN = a doctor specialising in children's health. Root: Greek paidos (child) + iatros (physician). Compare: geriatrician (elderly), cardiologist (heart), dermatologist (skin), neurologist (nervous system).

B is correct. ACROPHOBIA = irrational fear of heights (Greek: akros = at the top). Common phobia list: acrophobia (heights), claustrophobia (enclosed spaces), agoraphobia (open/public spaces), arachnophobia (spiders), hydrophobia (water), xenophobia (strangers/foreigners), nyctophobia (darkness).

questions.stem: One who does not believe in the existence of God.
questions.explanation: B is correct. ATHEIST = one who does not believe in God (a + theist; 'a' is Greek prefix meaning 'without'). Compare: theist (believes in personal God), deist (believes in creator God who doesn't intervene), agnostic (believes truth is unknowable). These distinctions are tested in SSC vocabulary sections.

questions.stem: A government run by a small group of people.
questions.explanation: C is correct. OLIGARCHY = rule by a few (Greek: oligos = few + arkhein = to rule). Government types: democracy (demos = people), monarchy (monos = one), oligarchy (few), theocracy (theos = god), plutocracy (wealth), autocracy (single unlimited power), bureaucracy (bureau = office). These are heavily tested.

questions.stem: A person who looks on the bright side of things.
questions.explanation: C is correct. OPTIMIST = a person who tends to see the best in things and expect favourable outcomes. Root: Latin optimus = best. Antonym: pessimist (expects worst). Related: optimism, optimistic. Easily confused with: cynic (not just negative — specifically distrusts human motives).

questions.stem: A person who pretends to be what he or she is not.
questions.explanation: B is correct. HYPOCRITE = a person who professes beliefs or virtues they do not actually possess; one who pretends to be what they are not. Charlatan is similar but specifically refers to false expertise. Sycophant = flatterer. Root: Greek hypokrits = actor on stage.

B is correct. FRATRICIDE = killing of one's brother (Latin frater = brother + -cide = killing). Common -cide words: fratricide (brother), sororicide (sister), patricide (father), matricide (mother), infanticide (infant), regicide (king), genocide (ethnic group), homicide (human), suicide (self).

questions.stem: A person who is indifferent to pleasure and pain.
questions.explanation: C is correct. STOIC = a person who can endure pain or hardship without showing feelings; indifferent to pleasure and pain. From Stoicism, the ancient Greek philosophy founded by Zeno. An ascetic avoids pleasure for spiritual purposes, but a stoic is characterised by emotional indifference to both pain and pleasure.

questions.stem: A person who has just started learning a subject.
questions.explanation: C is correct. NOVICE = a person new to and inexperienced in a job or situation; a beginner. Synonyms: beginner, neophyte, tyro, rookie, apprentice. Root: Latin novus = new. A prodigy has exceptional talent (not necessarily a beginner); a neophyte is a close synonym to novice.

questions.stem: A group of fish swimming together.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SHOAL (or SCHOOL) = a large group of fish swimming together. Collective nouns: shoal/school of fish, flock of birds, herd of cattle/elephants, pack of wolves, pride of lions, murder of crows, gaggle of geese, pod of whales/dolphins. These collective nouns are frequently tested.
